title: Japanese Wisteria: Ancient Wisteria Vines You Can Visit
meta_description: A climbing vine that can outlive most trees. Ushijima's Great Wisteria, roughly 1,200 years old, is the only one Japan protects at its highest rank.
intro: Japanese wisteria is a vine, and it can outlive almost any tree around it. The Great Wisteria of Ushijima, near Kasukabe, is put at roughly 1,200 years, four metres round at the base and trained across a trellis of 600 to 700 square metres; it is the only wisteria Japan protects as a Special Natural Monument, and the garden around it opens for about three weeks a year. At Yama-jinja, near Mount Fuji, two vines seeded themselves and climbed unassisted, granted national monument status in 1928. Ichinohe's vine, several hundred years old by local account, is untrained too. Tokyo's Kameido Tenjin wisteria has a claim stranger than its age: art historians trace a line from Hiroshige's 1856 print of it, arched drum bridge and all, to the wisteria Monet later planted at Giverny.
